The displacement map follows the element's real border-radius through an SDF, so capsules, circles and rounded rectangles bend along their own outline (refraction.js:100-117, 168-170).

States its limits honestly: no Apple refraction numbers, easing, toolbar height or concentric-radius formula, and invented values are labelled as such (SKILL.md:369-381, motion-accessibility.md:32-35).
Clearly separates the browser-support fallback from the user-preference fallback (SKILL.md:176-180; tokens.css:262-271).

Mirror copies are sanitised for accessibility: ids stripped, inert, tabindex=-1, aria-hidden (refraction.js:269-283).

Factual slip at SKILL.md:213-214: 'web pixels are smaller than points'. On Apple devices one CSS px maps to one UIKit point at default zoom, so the conversion rationale is wrong (the ~11px floor itself is harmless). Moderate confidence.

The contrast rule is taken from Apple and applied to the web without a WCAG caveat. 'Bold, any size 3:1' (SKILL.md:251-252; color.md:183; motion-accessibility.md:105) matches the HIG, but WCAG 2.x 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1 for bold text below about 14pt (18.66px). The web route can therefore produce WCAG failures.

Increase Contrast is discussed (SKILL.md:319-320) but never implemented for the web. tokens.css has no @media (prefers-contrast: more) or (forced-colors: active) block; its a11y section (lines 521-546) covers only reduced transparency and reduced motion.

Browser support for prefers-reduced-transparency is not documented. To my knowledge Safari, the browser Apple users would be on, does not support this media query, so the main fallback silently never fires there. Verify against current caniuse. refraction.js:69-72 does offer a manual data-rt hook, which is good.
SKILL.md:133 says refraction is 'never animated under Reduce Motion', but refraction.js has no prefers-reduced-motion check. The mirror-mode rAF tracking loop runs regardless (refraction.js:324-335).

Performance: mirror sync calls getBoundingClientRect twice per element on every frame indefinitely (refraction.js:306-335), with no IntersectionObserver or visibility pause. The displacement map is a per-pixel JS loop at CSS-pixel size (no devicePixelRatio) re-run on every ResizeObserver tick (120-156, 362-366), which risks jank during animated resizes and gives soft maps on HiDPI.

Dispersion compositing adds the alpha channel three times (refraction.js:223-236: each colour matrix keeps A, then arithmetic k2=k3=1). That is fine over an opaque backdrop but over-brightens alpha over semi-transparent backdrops. Low severity, inferred from the code.

Engine detection uses a UA-sniff allowlist (refraction.js:61-67) because CSS.supports('backdrop-filter','url(#a)') reports true in engines that do not render it. The reason is documented, but it is brittle as engines change, and there is no runtime feature probe.
No automated verification ships. Playwright verification is claimed (materials.md:142-146), but the fetched files include no test files, and WebKit/Safari is explicitly untested.

The SwiftUI coverage is thin: no glassEffectTransition or morph example, no backgroundExtensionEffect, scrollEdgeEffectStyle or tab-bar minimise APIs (grep returned none) even though the matching design concepts are discussed (materials.md:206-229).

Could not verify (it is past my knowledge): the 'macOS 27 Golden Gate' page quote checked 2026-09-27 (SKILL.md:72-78). The hairline numbers '0.5px at ~12% opacity' (SKILL.md:156) appear under a 'read off Apple's HIG' provenance claim (SKILL.md:36-41), but I know of no HIG source for them.
Scope is Apple-only. It does not cover WebGL/WebGPU refraction, generic glassmorphism design-system tokens beyond Apple, or a canvas/shader route for the web.
adoptable_ideas: Route by platform before giving any design advice, and split each platform's capability into Backdrop, Blur and Bend so the agent picks the right mechanism and fallback (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:references/platforms.md, lines 7-31).

An engine with several modes: live backdrop-filter url() where the engine renders it, a sanitised mirror-copy plus CSS filter for known static sources elsewhere, and a plain-blur no-op otherwise. Expose the mode per element (modeOf) and a root class, so CSS and tests can assert which path ran (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/refraction.js, lines 20-33, 355-391).

Build the displacement map from a signed distance field of the element's actual computed border-radius, with a bounded rim band (a fraction of the radius, capped as a share of the short side) and a softened map to avoid pinching at corners. Ours should add DPR awareness and a selectable physical surface profile (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/refraction.js, lines 100-218).

Chromatic dispersion via per-channel displacement passes at slightly different scales. Ours should handle alpha correctly (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/refraction.js, lines 220-236).
Cache the filter by a parameter key, and only rebuild when size, radius or options change (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/refraction.js, lines 185-188).
Lower the tint automatically while bending, with an opt-out class for glass that carries text (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/tokens.css, lines 308-334).

Keep two separate fallbacks: @supports-not for a missing capability and a media query for the user setting. Ours should add prefers-contrast: more, forced-colors, and a manual attribute override (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/tokens.css, lines 262-271, 525-546).

A rim drawn as a masked gradient ring (content-box exclude composite) instead of a uniform border, plus a separate specular sheen layer (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/tokens.css, lines 273-306).
An 'Honest gaps / provenance with dates' section that keeps invented numbers out of guidance attributed to Apple (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:SKILL.md, lines 350-381).

A review checklist made of concrete shipped mistakes (glass on content, more than one tinted element per bar, missing press state, no @supports fallback, no bend in non-Chromium browsers) that a review agent can run mechanically (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:SKILL.md, lines 324-348).

A visual test over a line of text and a straight-edged photo: rim letters should curve while the middle stays readable. Ours should automate this across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with screenshot diffs (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:references/materials.md, lines 157-161).

Sanitise mirror copies for accessibility (strip ids, inert, tabindex -1, aria-hidden) so duplicated DOM never reaches assistive tech or tab order (xenitV1/liquid-glass-skill@8cf508b2e547:assets/refraction.js, lines 264-283).

Ways to beat it: DPR-aware maps built in a worker or OffscreenCanvas, IntersectionObserver or visibility pausing of mirror sync, a WebGL/WebGPU route, dual Apple and WCAG contrast gates with a measuring script, prefers-contrast tokens, SwiftUI morph and transition recipes, and shipped automated tests.

adoptable_ideas: Geometry-keyed displacement-map cache: key = (w,h,radius,zoom,bezel) rounded, with in-flight promise dedupe and delayed GC of unused SVG filters (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 231-297).

Analytic bezel optics: superellipse height profile, Snell deviation per sample, offset = glass height * tan(incident - refracted), sampled once to find max for normalization (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 206-211); our engine should reimplement this with documented derivation and add an optional Fresnel/specular term.

Fold lens magnification into the same map as a linear radial term (px*(1-1/zoom)) so zoom costs nothing extra (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 245-249).

Chromatic dispersion as three displacement passes at scale*(1+d), scale, scale*(1-d), channel-isolated via feColorMatrix and recombined with screen blends, offered as an opt-in 'full' tier vs a single-pass 'lite' tier (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 256-257, 317-333).

Separate the rim-light highlight into a precomputed texture applied as a CSS background so the non-Chromium fallback still looks like glass, not just blur (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 237-242, 286).

Viewport-gated refraction: swap backdrop-filter between url(#filter)+blur and blur-only via IntersectionObserver with a pre-roll margin (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 267-272, 306).

Material contract: one host class plus an injected decorative layer at z-index:-1 inside an isolated host, with custom-property knobs per component and root-level global overrides (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 74-84, 277-279) - extend it with tokens instead of hard-coded theme colors.

A 'When NOT to use' section and an 'existing design = glass only' mode in the skill (the-Ashkanian/ashi-liquid-glass@1dc795bcceb8c475da75cb5167cb0f23b052da6a:SKILL.md lines 19-25, 44-46) - adopt, but make the question flow skippable with stated assumptions.

Beat it on: SwiftUI/UIKit glassEffect references, full Backdrop Root rule list, feature-test-plus-UA capability detection, contrast/legibility checks, reduced-transparency and forced-colors fallbacks, complete accessible interaction code, a destroy()/MutationObserver lifecycle, size-animation guidance, and a real-browser verification step with screenshots and perf budgets.

The iOS 26 SwiftUI APIs are `matchedTransitionSource(id:in:)` plus `.navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:))`, which the same repo's toolbar-patterns.md:62-81 uses correctly. This is an internal contradiction, and liquid-glass.md:401 repeats the non-existent `navigationZoomTransition` name.

FACTUAL/COMPILE ERROR: the glassEffectWithFallback helper (liquid-glass.md:376-390) takes a `Glass` parameter in a View extension that has no @available(iOS 26, *) annotation. With a deployment target below iOS 26, the signature itself fails to compile ('Glass is only available in iOS 26.0 or newer'), so the runtime #available check inside does not help.

MISLEADING: 'Both views must have the same glassEffectID' (liquid-glass.md:197). Apple's documented pattern gives each glass element its own ID within a shared namespace, and glass morphs as elements appear or disappear. Same-ID swapping is one technique, not a requirement. glassEffectTransition(_:) (.matchedGeometry/.materialize/.identity) is never mentioned.

INCOMPLETE SEMANTICS: GlassEffectContainer spacing 'should match the actual spacing in your layout' (liquid-glass.md:139, 416, 440). The parameter is the distance at which nearby glass shapes begin to blend or merge; the file never explains that, so an agent cannot reason about unintended merging.
